clue.text: Pseudo-analysed one''s hidden, difficult Freudian desire

indicators.note: something hidden is tucked away inside, so the following letter sits within the reworked word
to analyse is to break something down into parts, so the word before it is taken apart and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, then reworked
I is the Roman numeral for one
complex means complicated or hard

explanation.surface: A sham psychoanalysis uncovers someone's buried, troublesome Freudian urge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pseudo-analysed' looks like a single adjective, but the hyphen hides a word plus its signal. 'One's hidden' tells you the numeral goes inside the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud named the son's supposed desire for his mother after the Greek king who unknowingly married his own mother.

clue.text: Bad guy entertaining there in private

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest has them inside the house, so the outer pieces wrap around the next word

parts.note: food that has gone bad is off
taken as written
a guy is a rope or cord holding a tent steady

explanation.surface: A villain is hosting someone at a secret location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad guy' looks like one villain, but the two words give separate pieces, which wrap around the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks made off the record are confidential and not for publication, so they are spoken in private.

clue.text: Appliance obtained from doctor? That's right!

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
i.e. stands for id est, Latin for 'that is'
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone checks that an appliance came from a doctor and is told yes, correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's right!' reads as an exclamation of agreement, but it splits into 'that is' and 'right'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drier is a household machine for drying clothes or hair, so it is an appliance.

clue.text: Summon pervert there to see topless picture

parts.note: to page someone is to call for them over a loudspeaker or pager

indicators.note: to pervert is to twist or distort, so the following word has its letters bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then reworked

explanation.surface: Calling a deviant over to look at a racy photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: PAGE THREE was the page of the British tabloid the Sun that for decades carried a photograph of a topless model.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase came to stand for the topless glamour photograph that appeared on that newspaper page.

clue.text: Points to crude, debauched philanderer

parts.note: two compass points, south and east

indicators.note: something debauched is corrupted from its proper state, so the preceding word is corrupted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then reworked

explanation.surface: Someone singles out a coarse, dissolute womaniser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' is a crossword staple for compass directions, here south and east.
explanation.definitionFit: A seducer lures people into sexual relationships, much as a philanderer has casual affairs.

clue.text: US state capital hosted the Games many years ago

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the capital city of Washington state

definitions.text: hosted the Games many years ago
definitions.note: the answer is the place that hosted, a noun, not the verb
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the sanctuary in Greece where the ancient Olympic Games were held

explanation.surface: An American state capital once staged the Olympics.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a modern American host city, but the two halves point to two different places with one name.
explanation.definitionFit: Washington's capital shares its name with the ancient Greek site of the original Olympic festival.

clue.text: King taken in by lousy agent

indicators.note: being taken in means being drawn inside, so the first piece ends up within the second

parts.note: poxy is British slang for rubbish or worthless
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is fooled by a useless representative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' suggests being deceived, but here it means placed inside. Poxy is British slang for lousy or second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: A proxy is a person authorised to act or vote on behalf of another, which is what an agent does.

clue.text: After rough treatment, are able to give more information

indicators.note: handling something roughly knocks it out of shape, so the following words come out in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, then reworked

explanation.surface: Having been roughed up, prisoners can now tell their interrogators more.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate on something is to expand on it with extra detail.

clue.text: Shy fellow approaches Heather

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: A bashful man walks up to a woman called Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like an adjective describing the fellow, but it is a verb meaning throw, and Heather is the plant, not a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To shy something is to toss it, as at a coconut shy, and to fling is likewise to throw.

clue.text: Regularly write diary now without thought for the future

definitions.note: a cryptic description of the adverbial sense, not a synonym
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a diary is kept by writing up each day as it comes
second meaning: living only for the present

explanation.surface: Advice to keep a diary faithfully, set against living heedlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic hint: a diarist writes up one date after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living day-to-day deals only with the immediate present and makes no long-term plans.

clue.text: He appears to be virtuous, but bedaubs fine books

parts.note: to bedaub is to smear thickly, as one plasters
A1 means first-rate, written with I standing in for the one
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A sanctimonious man is exposed for defacing good books.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means excellent; the digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaster saint is someone presented as morally flawless, a hollow image of goodness rather than the real thing.

clue.text: Eric, the crazy dissident

indicators.note: something crazy is in a disordered state, so the preceding words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then reworked

explanation.surface: Eric is a mad rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretic holds views at odds with established doctrine, just as a dissident rejects official policy.

clue.text: Profit, turnover and total wage bill

parts.note: if something profits you, it pays
a roll is a turning over, as a dog rolls over

explanation.surface: A firm's accounts list profit, turnover and staff costs.
explanation.walkthrough: The business vocabulary is a decoy: 'turnover' is a physical roll, not sales revenue.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm's payroll is the list of employees and the total sum paid to them in wages.

clue.text: He gets up a vertical pipe

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who gets out of bed, as an early one
second meaning: an upright pipe carrying water or gas between floors

explanation.surface: A man climbs up a drainpipe.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a burglar shinning up a pipe, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An early riser leaves bed promptly, and in plumbing a riser is the upright supply pipe.

clue.text: Standing next to Queen (old rock group)

parts.note: one's standing in society is one's status
QU is an abbreviation for queen
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: One band is ranked alongside Queen, a veteran rock act.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen in the surface is the band, which makes 'rock group' look like a gloss on it; in fact Queen gives QU and the definition is the other band.
explanation.definitionFit: Status Quo is a long-running British rock band, known for boogie hits such as Rockin' All Over the World.

clue.text: Comes back to harvest fruit

parts.note: to reap is to gather in a crop
pears are a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone returns each autumn to pick the orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappear is to show up again after an absence, which is to return.

clue.text: Plan for king to meet a married Frenchwoman

parts.note: pro means in favour of
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
taken as written
Mme is the abbreviation for Madame, a married Frenchwoman's title

explanation.surface: Arrangements are made for a monarch to have a rendezvous with a Frenchman's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: GR is the royal cipher of King George, seen on old British postboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme is a schedule of intended events, which is a plan.

clue.text: "Take care of her", Capone ordered

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so the preceding words are set out afresh

parts.note: taken as written, then reworked
taken as written, then reworked

explanation.surface: The gangster Al Capone instructs a henchman to deal with a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: In gangster talk 'take care of her' is a threat; here it means look after.
explanation.definitionFit: To chaperone someone is to accompany and supervise them, a protective way of looking after them.

clue.text: Round tables designed for monks

parts.note: the letter O is round

indicators.note: something designed is newly arranged to a plan, so the word before it is laid out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then reworked

explanation.surface: Circular refectory tables are made for a monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round tables' reads as one item of furniture, but 'Round' is just the shape of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblates are people dedicated to religious life in a monastery, often as lay members alongside monks.

clue.text: Bergamo's suffering a commercial stoppage

indicators.note: a place that is suffering is in a bad way, so the name before it is battered out of shape

parts.note: taken as written, then reworked

explanation.surface: The Italian city of Bergamo is hit by a halt to trade.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban on trade with a country, which halts commerce.

clue.text: Too fat to be seen inside

indicators.note: the answer is found within the run of words, sitting in the middle of them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word through most of the last

explanation.surface: Someone is too overweight to be seen in public.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means extremely overweight, well past a healthy size.

clue.text: About to take lead from extremely large window

parts.note: round and about both mean around

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its front, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone is about to remove the lead from a huge window, as in leaded glazing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely large' reads as one phrase meaning huge, but 'extremely' only supplies its first letter and 'large' its usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundel is a small circular window or panel of glass, so it is a kind of window.

clue.text: Sir Francis died a roué!

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
a roué and a rake are both dissolute pleasure-seekers

explanation.surface: A scandalous obituary: Sir Francis died a libertine.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan sea captain who sailed around the world and fought the Spanish Armada.
explanation.definitionFit: The knighted Elizabethan explorer was Francis Drake, so his title and first name identify him.

clue.text: Retired wife yearns for good scores on the golf course

definitions.text: good scores on the golf course

indicators.note: to retire is to go back or withdraw, so the following word is read in the backward direction

parts.note: a wife is jokingly called a rib, after Eve's creation from Adam's rib
one who is dying for something yearns for it

explanation.surface: A pensioner's wife longs for her husband to post good golf scores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired wife' suggests a pensioner, but 'Retired' only turns the next word round. Rib for wife is an old jocular term from Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: A birdie is a hole completed in one stroke under par, a good result in golf.

clue.text: 24 Woman caught in wire netting

indicators.note: something caught in a net is trapped within it, so the answer is held within the following words

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A woman is trapped in a wire fence.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray 24 at the start is the clue's own number repeated in the source and plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a woman's given name, and crosswords freely define names by 'woman' or 'girl'.

clue.text: Comparatively short, thickset person sitting on his heels

definitions.meaning: first meaning: more squat, the comparative of an adjective meaning short and stocky
second meaning: one who crouches down with the haunches resting on the heels

explanation.surface: A description of a stocky little man crouching down.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one portrait, but the first half is an adjective in the comparative and the second a noun for someone crouching.
explanation.definitionFit: Squat means short and broad, so squatter is the comparative; and a squatter is also one who squats on the heels.

clue.text: African president once presented honour to grand individual

parts.note: MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
a grand is a thousand pounds, written K
I is a single one, like the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A former African leader awarded a British honour to a distinguished person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand individual' looks like an eminent person, but splits in two. The MBE is a British royal honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Thabo Mbeki succeeded Nelson Mandela as president of South Africa, serving from 1999 to 2008.

clue.text: Feminism has written off the opposition!

parts.note: surface reading: a campaign has dismissed its opponents
setter's reading: the opposite sex, men, have been struck out of a longer word, leaving the female form, which then moves

explanation.surface: A boast that feminism has seen off its critics.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the joke: write the word for men, strike them off a longer word, and what is left is the female form, set in motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Feminism is the campaign for women's rights, known collectively by this name since the 1960s.
